reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that raw kicker success rates are noisy and unreliable without sufficient sample sizes. Shrinkage estimation addresses this by borrowing strength from the league-wide distribution while preserving kicker-specific variation. The model assumes that each kicker's true ability varies around a common mean, with variance inversely proportional to sample size. Distance-dependent modeling captures the monotonic decline in success probability with increasing yardage. The inclusion of stadium effects acknowledges that environmental conditions can significantly alter performance expectations. These primitives form a coherent Bayesian network where each component contributes to a robust prediction of field goal outcomes.
